hints.title: Majority Element Bottleneck
hints.text: Pairs must have strictly different values. Any value cannot be paired with an identical value.

hints.title: Bisection Frequency Search
hints.text: Because nums is sorted, if a majority element exists, it must occupy the middle index n // 2.

hints.title: Leftover Math
hints.text: Let max_freq be the maximum frequency. If max_freq > n // 2, leftover elements equal 2 * max_freq - n, otherwise n % 2.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def minLengthAfterRemovals(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        mid = nums[n // 2]
        left = bisect_left(nums, mid)
        right = bisect_right(nums, mid)
        max_freq = right - left
        if max_freq > n // 2:
            return 2 * max_freq - n
        return n % 2
```

variables: n: length of sorted nums array
complexity.notes: Binary search for majority element boundaries in sorted array.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Greedy simulation using priority queue takes O(n log n).
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use median frequency analysis to determine remaining count in O(log n).
